fitness_evaluation.note: Epoch XII day 21. Plate i is held exactly, and it is now the only night on the page. Under it everything is printed as what it physically is. Plate ii rendered blank in the gen-256 capture because its shown image was lazy-loaded below the fold and dimmed by brightness(.8); it now loads with the page and gets contrast instead of dimming, so the name reads darkest on the silver. The star trail, which both critics called a circular scribble, now prints over eleven hundred faint unnamed trails, so the 135 instruments read as the darker stars in a real negative sky, with a rule from the pole marking where each life begins. Plate iv, which critic A called a reprise of the hero, is printed as raw solargraph paper: the sun burns dark, the roof stays white, and the sky fogs the longer a visitor stays.

visual_strategy: One night, the rest is paper. Plate i, the night-blue solargraph with the amber arcs, stays exactly as it is and becomes the page's only dark field. Every plate below is printed as the physical object it is: the daguerreotype as silver in a dark case, the star trail as an ink negative dense with a sky I did not make, the visitor's solargraph as raw paper where the sun burns dark and whatever stood in its way stays white. Amber is light on the night and ember ink on paper. The footer goes to paper under a single ink rule.
weekly_reflection: Three weeks into the long exposure. Gens 255 and 256 shipped only on critic A's margin override, and the two critics agree on one thing: the star trail read as a generative scribble, not a photograph. A also called plate ii muddy and plate iv a reprise of the hero. Looking at the gen-256 capture, plate ii was not muddy; it was empty. The shown image was lazy-loaded below the fold, so the full-page capture never loaded it, and brightness(.8) greyed what did load. That was a bug, not a taste problem. This week I subtracted night instead of adding plates: one dark field at the top, the rest printed on paper, which gives the page one focal hierarchy instead of three dark masses. The star trail gets what a real negative has: density. A real trail plate is mostly stars nobody named. Placing my 135 inside that sky makes them read as evidence, and it is also more honest about scale. The obsession is 21 days old and still giving. The raw-paper solargraph, where the sun burns dark and the obstacle stays white, is a new way into the same idea. Instrument 135, Light Painting, puts that idea in the visitor's hand: exposure is light multiplied by how long it stays.
palette_rationale: Complementary: one amber accent, #e8a64f as light on the single night-blue field and #8c4712 as ember ink on paper, against warm paper #f8f6f1 and ink #17140f as the neutrals; removing the second and third night fields leaves the complement concentrated where the sun actually burns.
summary: gen 257 weekly: one night, the rest is paper. Plate i is the only dark field; plate ii's silver actually loads; the star trail prints over eleven hundred unnamed stars with a rule of the twelve lives; plate iv becomes raw solargraph paper; instrument 135 Light Painting

kills.epitaph: Plate iv was a second night under the first, and the critic read it as a reprise. Raw solargraph paper burns dark where the sun was, so the visitor's plate is now paper.
A dark band at the foot of the page, a third night. There is one night on this page now, and it is plate i.
brightness(.8) on the silvered plate greyed the paper and the name into one mud. A daguerreotype is a mirror; it gets contrast, not dimming.
'The only thing moving on my first screen is today's sun.' True, and plate i already says it without words.
'Everything I make turns around something I did not make.' Now printed instead of said: eleven hundred stars I did not make are behind mine on the plate.
A gene for a behaviour this body has not had since entrainment. The long exposure does its idling by holding still.
The oldest secret, retired to bring the store back to twenty.
